::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Aug 12 [1899]  
**From:** The Old House Dorking  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels/78
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd)
I am glad there are some signs of life or of decay more properly of poor [A D I](people/person_744.qmd)- !  I do think there are more and more signs that a 6d phoenix would be welcomed.[^1]

I find the booksellers make all sorts of excuses for not having got it –  The [Authors Soc](organizations/other_44.qmd) want to see my agreement before advising me.  I could not find it easily before I left home and was too hot for a hunt.  [FMP](people/person_1160.qmd) has written to offer a visit on the 17th or 18th so I have written to her to meet me and come with me on the 18th  I have got the MS of [Ducks Eggs](cmy_books/cmybook_251.qmd), I think I can make them much more interesting and longer.  We are nice and cool here now, but I think people must suppose that I dispose of all the [scholarship](organizations/other_113.qmd) money for the begging letters are endless.  [Anna Bramston](people/person_195.qmd) has photographed all the tableaux before the break up!  Poor [George](people/person_1610.qmd) at Kimberley is tormented as nephew to a lion, and was invited to go to a book dance as ‘[The Daisy Chain](cmy_books/cmybook_24.qmd)’- pretty well for a great black police officer.  So you may tell [Walter](people/person_353.qmd) to prepare to be invited out as Jack a Lantern.  [Helen](people/person_1613.qmd) returns remembrances.  I have had a charming letter from the old [Mignonette](people/person_1637.qmd) about Maximilian and the Martinswand- and an Italian palace – quite good enough for an article. [^2]  The local demon [Mr ffinch](people/person_1688.qmd) & co are a great success, he reads the lessons so beautifully that I am quite sorry to miss a fortnight of him.  He is warden of a college for ‘decayed gentlewomen’  I should think you would have heard of it.

[Maurice](people/person_1630.qmd) and [Maude](people/person_1629.qmd) have the funniest little cottage at Fleet, in the middle of purple heath

your affectionate
C M Yonge

Poor Lanty!

---

[^1]: They were hoping that the *[MP](organizations/other_52.qmd)* would be revived in a cheaper form.
[^2]: The legend that the emperor Maximilian I (1459-1519) climbed the Martinswand near Innsbruck is referred to in CMY’s novel *The Dove in the Eagle’s Nest* (1866) and is also the subject of one of Schubert’s songs.
